# http/deliver

A built-in deliver adapter for person records: it needs the step's `uses:` fields and declares no fields of its own. It publishes no per-record estimate, so plan prints `?`, and it demands no credential.

## Manifest

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| id | `http/deliver` |
| version | 1 |
| role | deliver |
| entity type | person |
| credentials | none |
| cost estimate per record | not published |

## Needs

The fields the step's `uses:` line names, and nothing else.

## Provides

Nothing; a delivery row is what it writes.

## Config keys

The keys `with:` accepts. Plan rejects any other key.

| Key | Type | Required | What it sets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth` | object |  |  |
| `auth.env` | string | yes |  |
| `auth.name` | string |  |  |
| `auth.prefix` | string |  |  |
| `auth.type` | one of header, query, bearer, basic | yes |  |
| `body` | any |  | Body template; default is the resolved variables object |
| `entity_type` | string |  |  |
| `headers` | object |  |  |
| `keep_payloads` | boolean |  |  |
| `method` | one of POST, PUT, PATCH |  | Default POST |
| `query` | object |  |  |
| `url` | string | yes | Target URL; may template {{record.\<field\>}} / {{config.*}} |
| `variables` | object |  | Egress mapping, injected by the runner from the step-level variables: key. |

## Example

A minimal step:

```yaml
  - id: deliver
    use: http/deliver
```
